newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil FCVS '97 debt issues won't top 8 bln reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil FCVS '97 debt issues won't top 8 bln reais.

text.p: Brazil's National Treasury is not expected to issue more than eight billion reais in debt in 1997 to cover a shortfall in a federal housing fund, said Sergio Cutolo, president of federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica.

"We don't have as yet a precise estimate, but the Treasury is not expected to issue next year anything above eight billion reais," Cutolo told reporters during a news conference to launch a securitization plan for the so-called FCVS housing fund.

Saying Brazil was taking one of its last fiscal skeletons out of the closet, Finance Minister Pedro Malan told reporters earlier that the government had identified 17.7 billion reais as concrete debt that would have to be securitized.
Cutolo said that the Caixa Economica and the Treasury hoped to reduce this sum considerably through a program of refinancing federal mortgages and early retirement of mortgages.
"This will permit the government to reduce considerably the potential deficit of the FCVS," Cutolo said.

He added that for example, the Caixa Economica held eight billion reais in FCVS mortgages, but that the amount could be reduced by three billion reais by swapping it for another type of mortgage paper held by the Caixa.

He said the government had also identified numerous mortgage holders who were inappropriately holding more than one FCVS-backed contract and that the government would only assume responsibility for one.

As for FCVS debt which has not yet been recognized, Cutolo said the government expected to reduce this through a program of incentives for mortgage holders to pay off their mortgages early. By offering this incentive, the Caixa could reduce its potential loss by up to 70 percent, Cutolo said.
